headline: The Energy Department has offered Vistra a conditional loan of up to $4.2 billion to boost output at three nuclear plants, including Perry in Ohio.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: the department's own announcement with figures, still conditional; the 150,000-homes figure comes from Cleveland.com alone.
importance_line: Households and businesses on the 13-state PJM grid (about 67 million people) are told the loan will lower bills and prevent outages, but it is conditional, the extra 433 megawatts is already sold to Meta, and the Perry work is not due before 2031.
summary: POWER Magazine reports that the US Energy Department announced on Monday 5 Oct 2026 a conditional commitment of up to $4.2 billion in loans to Vistra, a Texas-based power producer, to fund uprates (upgrades that let a reactor produce more power) at its Perry and Davis-Besse plants in Ohio and Beaver Valley plant in Pennsylvania; the department says the work could add 433 megawatts of capacity (a megawatt is a million watts) and support 20 more years of operation beyond the plants' current licenses. This makes official the loan plan Bloomberg reported from unnamed sources, which we carried in our 3 Oct edition, though Vistra must still meet technical, legal, environmental and financial conditions before any money is lent; Cleveland.com reports Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the Perry work alone would add enough power for 150,000 homes.
notes: Cleveland.com (pool link) returned 403, so the entry is built from POWER Magazine, WSYX and energytech.com, which agree. The 150,000-homes figure is from Cleveland.com's headline only and is attributed to it. Follow-up of item 40 of our 3 Oct 2026 edition (Bloomberg, about $4 billion, unnamed sources); the event itself, the announcement at Perry, is 5 Oct 2026.
